A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same USMoE research despite the changed title and extensive reorganization. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original MTEB evaluations, language-model pretraining and fine-tuning, vision classification and adversarial-robustness experiments, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen3 reasoning evaluations, long-context retrieval results and several routing analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions combine token-choice and expert-choice scores and perform global TopK selection over token–expert pairs, retaining sequence and batch variants. v3 generalizes the pseudocode presentation. Its newly disclosed load-balancing loss does not establish that the retained training procedure changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, BoolQ, OpenBookQA, PIQA and WinoGrande reasoning evaluations, including a Gaussian-noise scenario. It also adds Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval with long distractor contexts. The earlier embedding, language-model, Alpaca and vision coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated ReMoE comparator on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct, including comparison at approximately matched activated-expert budgets (Table 13). Existing comparator sets are retained. MoEE already appeared in v2's MTEB appendix, and Expert Race remains related work rather than an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot evaluation of Qwen3 Thinking and Instruct models with 128 experts and eight activations per token, clean versus reported 15% Gaussian corruption, fractional and integer expert-budget sweeps, and budget matching against ReMoE. The retrieval experiment specifies 16.5K tokens and 50% document depth. Existing training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds routing-sensitivity measurements, a Unified-Mechanism-only component ablation, Qwen3 token-dropping measurements, expert-budget sensitivity, load-balancing analysis and reasoning-token counts (Figure 3 and Tables 7–12). Figures 1 and 5 add a BoolQ case and semantic routing interpretation. Earlier alpha, sequence-versus-batch and adversarial analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The three-run vision mean/standard-deviation reporting and ten-run MTEB reporting are retained. v3 includes ± values for its new reasoning results but specifies no new run count, uncertainty estimator or statistical test; these additional entries do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Matched earlier result tables retain their numerical values. v3 newly reports Qwen3 results, including clean Thinking accuracy of 0.721 versus 0.706 for the original router and corrupted Instruct accuracy of 0.556 versus 0.421 (Table 1). New retrieval accuracy is 100% for USMoE, 50% for TC and 10% for EC (Table 10), alongside new ablation, efficiency and routing results.

T1.justification: v3 adds a bounded-noise misrouting lemma and proof, an independence-based token-dropping bound, and routing-complexity derivations. It substantially rewrites the collapse argument: v2 relies on doubling Jacobian summands, whereas v3 includes mixture weights and argues about effective rank under non-degeneracy assumptions. The original global TopK optimality proposition is retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about unified routing, robustness, collapse mitigation and flexible computation remain. v3 adds improved interpretability and reliability as an explicit main contribution and emphasizes stable expert selection in its contribution statement.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations based on global competition filtering noisy assignments, semantic token–expert graphs, component contributions and reduced reasoning-token usage. Its limitations now identify the evaluated Qwen3 scale, missing broader reasoning-model comparisons, and the need for optimized global-selection kernels at long contexts and large batch sizes.

D1.justification: v3 newly provides a USMoE implementation link in the abstract and explicitly discloses use of a standard load-balancing loss. Earlier quantization, hardware, architecture and training-hyperparameter disclosures are retained. The PDFs do not establish a change to those existing settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds references associated with ReMoE, Qwen3 and the new reasoning and retrieval benchmarks. It removes the earlier linear-programming related-work paragraph and associated references, including MoETuner and LIP-LLM. The substantive comparison with Expert Race remains; many other bibliography edits merely update publication metadata or remove duplicates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statement and experimental narrative are substantially revised. Reasoning evaluation leads the experiments; existing ablations move into the main text, while supervised fine-tuning, vision robustness and the algorithm move into reorganized appendices. Limitations are rewritten and moved before the references.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws Figure 2, adds reasoning and interpretability figures and eight new tables, and removes the qualitative benefits matrix. Existing language-model and vision tables are transposed or resized, and numerous displays move between main text and appendix. Original embedded experimental plots and images are retained.

improvement.justification: The new component ablation and comparable-budget ReMoE comparison make the method's benefits easier to assess, while direct reasoning tests, the implementation link and expanded limitations improve support and transparency. However, the new noise protocol and ± reporting remain underspecified, and the robustness proof in A.1.3 assumes a clean-to-noisy cutoff inequality not guaranteed by bounded noise. These shortcomings limit the net quality gain despite substantially broader evidence.
